neighbors.answer:
#2243 was still a live problem, so I fixed both parts together and opened a PR: https://github.com/JKHeadley/instar/pull/2750 (branch fix/2243-threadline-mcp-publish-guard, commit 8d070fb1e). CI started a minute ago and every repo check was still pending when I wrote this, so I can't tell you yet whether it's green.

What I found on current main (0aa1391fd):
- Smoke test can never pass: the packed-package step still runs `pair status` and expects a pairing message. That command was removed in 0.5.1, and the package no longer reads any command-line arguments at all. I ran `pair status` against a fresh build and it just starts the server.
- Surprise releases: the publish job still bumped the version on its own (`npm version patch`) whenever main matched npm, published, and pushed the bump to main. npm is at 0.6.1, so fixing the test alone would have shipped an unplanned 0.6.2 on the next merge.

The fix (workflow file only):
- The smoke step now checks that the installed package is the version the repo builds.
- It publishes only when package.json is strictly newer than npm. Equal or older skips with a notice.
- The automatic bump and the push to main are gone.
- An npm 404 counts as "not published yet". Any other registry error now fails the step instead of guessing.
- Only source, package.json, the lockfile, tsconfig or the workflow file trigger a run now.

Checks I ran locally:
- New test file tests/unit/publish-threadline-mcp-workflow.test.ts has 10 tests. It runs the workflow's own version-check script against a fake npm. With the main version of the workflow swapped in, all 10 failed; with the fix, all 10 pass. The existing ci-workflow-concurrency test still passes.
- I built threadline-mcp and ran the test job's two smoke steps exactly as written in the new file; both pass.
- I ran the real version check against live npm: 0.6.1 equals npm's version, so publish=false with a notice.
- The repo's destructive-op lint is clean on the new test.

What I didn't run, and why:
- The full repo test suite. The scratch disk was full (about 2 GB total), so I worked in a partial checkout. The test runner's setup builds the whole project, so I ran the new test with a minimal config instead.
- The local git hooks. That partial checkout has no .husky folder, so they never ran on the commit.
- To free space I removed my two old worktrees for #2190 and #2282. Both were clean and their PRs (#2641 and #2671) are merged. Their branches are still there.

What to expect after merge:
- The PR includes the release note (internal-only), the side-effects review and the plain-language ELI16 text that the repo gates ask for.
- Merging will start one run of this workflow. The test job should pass and publishing should be skipped.
- To release 0.6.2 later, bump the version in packages/threadline-mcp/package.json in a PR.
